# Enemies should be aware of the wrap around

## Problem statement

Enemies are currently "wrap-blind": aimed shots always fire a straight line at
the player's raw position (never crossing a screen edge), and enemy movement is
bounded or clamped to the arena, so no enemy ever flies over a screen edge the
way the player ship, asteroids, bullets and the raider patrol already do. The
playfield seam is therefore one-directional — only the player's shots and the
player can cross it — letting the player camp the edges with impunity. Enemy
behaviour should be wrap-aware by default — firing across the seam to reach the
player and flying over the edges — controlled by a per-enemy parameter so a
small set of classic arcade archetypes (Space Invaders march, Centipede) keeps
its bounded, wall-respecting behaviour.

## Users

- **Players** — enemy shots can now arrive from anywhere, including from
  "off-screen" across the seam, so camping a screen edge is no longer a safe
  position. Most enemies occupy the whole wrap-around world rather than a
  bounded box, while the classic set pieces (Space Invaders, Centipede) stay
  recognisible.
- **AI agents / human developers** — one unambiguous data-driven per-archetype
  parameter (`wrapAware`, default `true`) that the game and every gym read
  through the same shared seams, so game↔gym parity is preserved by
  construction and tuning an archetype is a one-field change.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want enemies to fire at me across the screen edge, so that
  hiding against an edge is no longer a guaranteed safe position and shots can
  arrive from the seam exactly like my own wrapped bullets.
- As a **player**, I want most enemies to fly over a screen edge and reappear on
  the opposite side, so the whole wrapped playfield — not a bounded box — is
  part of the arena.
- As a **player**, I want the Space Invaders block and the Centipede to keep
  their classic behaviour (reversing at the walls / weaving within the arena),
  so those recognisable set pieces remain intact.
- As a **developer**, I want a single data-driven `wrapAware` parameter per
  archetype (default: aware) that behaves identically in the game and every
  gym, so enabling or disabling seam-awareness is a one-field change with no
  divergent copies.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Parameter** — Each enemy archetype carries a data-driven boolean
   `wrapAware` (or equivalently named) parameter, defaulting to `true`, wired
   through the existing `EnemyConfig` pipeline so it is visible and editable in
   the enemy editor panel. The `march` (Space Invaders) and `centipede` seed
   configs set it to `false`.
2. **Seam-aware aimed fire** — Aimed shots (Scout, march and the raider's
   aimed fire — every archetype routed through the aimed-shot method) fire
   along the shortest wrapped path to the player: when the direct line is
   longer than the wrap-around route, the shot leaves one edge and arrives from
   the opposite edge (enemy bullets already wrap; AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0). An
   enemy with `wrapAware: false` keeps the current direct aim.
3. **Wrap-aware movement** — Wrap-aware enemy motion (dive, chase, orbit,
   drift, roam, hold-and-move, etc.) that would carry the enemy off-screen
   wraps to the opposite edge (matching the player/asteroid four-edge wrap
   model) instead of being clamped. Non-aware archetypes (`march`,
   `centipede`) are unchanged: march reverses and drops at the arena edge;
   centipede weaves within bounds.
4. **Gym ↔ game parity** — The behaviour is implemented once in the shared
   core (`src/scenes/core/`) and exercised by the affected gym scene(s) and
   `PlayScene` in the same change, so the repo-wide duplicate-body / parity
   guards stay green.
5. **Testing, validation & docs** — Unit tests cover: seam-aware aim angle for
   wrap-aware enemies vs. direct aim for non-aware enemies; position wrapping
   on crossing each edge for wrap-aware motion; config default / CSV wiring
   including the `march` / `centipede` exclusions. The affected documentation
   (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` and any config-format docs) is
   updated to reflect the change. The full project test suite passes with the
   new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the bullet wrap model itself — enemy bullets already wrap and
  expire by lifetime (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0); this item changes launch direction
  and enemy movement only.
- Exclusions are an explicit seed-config list: only `march` and `centipede`
  default to non-aware. During planning, any other archetype whose classic
  design requires wall interaction belongs in the exclusion list, recorded as a
  code comment and a documented divergence per the gym↔game parity convention
  (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- Implement through the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`), never a divergent
  copy, so the game and every gym run the same code.
- Out of scope: boss behaviours, player ship, minerals, drops, and the bullet
  wrap model itself.
- Written in UK English per repo convention.

## Existing state

- Enemy aimed fire: `Scout.tryFireAimedBullet` computes
  `heading = atan2(target.y - y, target.x - x)` on **raw** positions with no
  seam consideration — the same aimed-shot method is reused for march and
  raider via `ENEMY_FIRE_METHODS` (`src/entities/enemyFire.ts`).
- Enemy bullets: wrap all four screen edges and expire by lifetime
  (AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0; shared bullet path in `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`).
- Enemy movement: bounded. Ghost/Grunt clamp to `GAME_WIDTH`/`GAME_HEIGHT`;
  march reverses and drops at arena bounds (`src/scenes/core/marchFormation.ts`:
  `computeMarchBounds` / `advanceMarch`); centipede weaves within bounds;
  formation drift pushes rightward.
- Wrap model to match: player ship and `Asteroid.updatePosition` four-edge
  wrap; `Raider` patrol already wraps; `LaneTraffic` wraps horizontally.
- Enemies are data-driven: `EnemyConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`) + seed
  defaults (`src/core/configDefaults.ts`) + CSV (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`)
  + enemy editor panel + gym editor.

## Desired change

1. Add the boolean parameter to `EnemyConfig` (`wrapAware`), seed default
   `true`; set `march` and `centipede` to `false`.
2. Seam-aware aim: for wrap-aware entities, compute the player delta along the
   shortest wrapped path before `atan2` in the shared aimed-fire seam; used by
   Scout / march / raider aimed fire (and any other archetype sharing the
   aimed-shot method).
3. Shared post-motion edge wrap: in the shared scene entity loop (game +
   gyms), wrap each wrap-aware enemy's position when it crosses an edge; gate
   on the flag so non-aware archetypes are untouched.
4. Verify per-archetype that nothing breaks (divers mid-dive, chasers,
   orbiters, swarm, formation drift) and adjust tests.
5. Update key docs (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; config-format
   docs if they enumerate fields).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add `wrapAware?: boolean` to `EnemyConfig`.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — seed defaults: `true` for most archetypes;
  `false` for `march` and `centipede`.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — new `wrapAware` column entries (if the CSV
  persists the field).
- `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` + aimed-fire call sites (`Scout.tryFireAimedBullet`,
  march, `Raider`) — seam-aware aim.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — expose the flag and any shared seam support.
- `src/scenes/core/` — shared post-motion wrap (CombatCoreScene / CombatScene
  shared entity loop, alongside the `enemyTargeting.ts` seams).
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` + affected gym scenes
  (`GymFodderEnemies`, `GymCentipede`, …) — parity exercises.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — document the parameter and the
  exclusions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: gameplay feel** — seam-aware aimed fire lets shots come from
  unexpected directions; mitigated by limiting the change to aimed shots
  (radial/spread remain direction-symmetric) and excluding the classic
  archetypes.
- **Risk: wrap × state-machine interaction** — a post-motion wrap applied to
  every wrap-aware archetype could interact with steering that seeks the player
  or with dive/common state machines near the seam (oscillation). Mitigation:
  per-archetype verification during planning and dedicated unit tests at the
  seam.
- **Risk: formation-drift scope** — drift formations that push off-screen wrap
  at the entity level; formation *bases* and shaping logic stay as-is.
- **Scope-creep guard** — seam-aware spread/radial patterns (Q2 option b) are
  out of scope; if wanted later they are tracked as a new work item, not added
  here. Any extra archetype exclusion discovered during planning becomes a new
  work item or is documented as a divergence, not silent scope growth.
- **Assumption: config plumbing** — the parameter lives in `EnemyConfig`
  (CSV-backed, editor-editable), consistent with the established data-driven
  enemy tooling; default `true` for all archetypes except the explicit
  exclusions.

## Related work

- **AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0** — "Bullets should have a distance and should wrap
  around the screen" (completed). Bullets already wrap; this item builds
  directly on that model for launch direction.
- **AH-0MV8BSMXC0097KLW** — "Enemies should emerge from the wormhole" (open).
  Touches the same shared enemy spawn/motion seams; potential overlap to watch
  during planning.
- **AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52** — "Extract common enemy base class for regular
  enemies" (completed). `BaseEnemy` hosts the shared config/seam support.
- **AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN** — "Enemy Design tooling" (completed). The
  data-driven `EnemyConfig` pipeline this parameter extends.
- **AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6** — "Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md
  best-practice guide" (completed). The doc updated by AC 5.
- **AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1** — gym↔game parity convention (referenced in
  `AGENTS.md`), enforced by `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Movement scope: which enemies should actually 'fly over the edge'? (a)
  All wrap-aware archetypes — shared post-motion wrap in scene loops;
  march/centipede excluded. (b) Firing only. (c) A curated subset."
  — Answer (Map): "(a)". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.
- Q2: "Firing scope: which fire patterns become seam-aware? (a) Aimed shots
  only. (b) All patterns."
  — Answer (Map): "(a)". Source: interactive reply, intake round 1.

# Audio Design Chapter — retro-arcade survival game GDD

## Problem statement

The GDD currently defines only SFX (§7.3 Audio Direction) and states background music is out of MVP scope with no musical direction defined. The game lacks a documented musical identity (scales, motifs, harmonic language, instrumentation, dynamic mixing, and state-driven music architecture) to guide composition and implementation when music is eventually built.

## Users

- **Audio designers and composers** — need a definitive musical language (scales/modes, motifs, progressions, instrumentation palette) to write consistent, on-brief music.
- **Technical audio programmers** — need the implementation contract (bus architecture, priority tiers, ducking, state machine, middleware guidance) to build or integrate the music system.
- **Game designers / producers** — need per-game-state emotional targets and transition rules to keep audio aligned with gameplay pacing.

User stories:

- As an audio designer, I want documented scales and motifs per game state, so my compositions match the game's emotional arc without guesswork.
- As a technical audio programmer, I want the music state machine and dynamic-mixing rules defined, so I can implement or configure the music engine against a fixed contract.
- As a producer, I want music explicitly scoped as design reference (out of MVP), so the shipped SFX scope (§7.3) is not disturbed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — New chapter file created:** An **AI Hell Music System** chapter is saved as a Markdown GDD addendum at `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`. Its **musical substance** is taken from the producer's original *Music & Thematic Audio Design* brief (Phrygian Dominant + Lydian scales; Combat Motifs A and B and the ambient "Star Drift" motif; the combat, boss and ambient progressions; the FM 2–4 operator + chiptune implementation notes — reproduced under **Source material (A)** below) and laid out in the **8-section + 2-appendix** professional structure of the approved reference brief (Ross, v1.0, 16 October 2026): **1** Audio Vision Statement; **2** Musical Identity (2.1 Tonal Language, 2.2 Core Motifs, 2.3 Chord Progressions); **3** Instrumentation Palette; **4** Dynamic Mixing Rules; **5** State-Driven Music Transitions (5.1 Transition Design Principles, 5.2 Transition Matrix, 5.3 Stinger System); **6** Implementation Guidelines (6.1 Audio Middleware, 6.2 Music Event Architecture, 6.3 Parameter Mapping Table, 6.4 Technical Specifications, 6.5 Audio Budget Table); **7** Composer and Sound Designer Briefs (7.1 Composer Brief, 7.2 Sound Designer Brief); **8** Audio Accessibility; **Appendix A** Motif Reference Sheet; **Appendix B** Glossary. The reference brief is a **structure exemplar only** — its Tableau card-game substance (D Dorian, harpsichord/cello ensemble, card-table SFX, parlour ambience) must **not** be imported into AI Hell's chapter.
- [ ] **AC2 — GDD §7.3 references the chapter:** The "Background Music" subsection in GDD §7.3 (Audio Direction) is updated to link the new chapter file, while retaining the explicit statement that background music is **out of MVP scope** (design reference only; SFX remains the only in-scope audio).
- [ ] **AC3 — GDD §8 future-scope row updated:** The "Background music" row in §8 (Future Scope) references the new chapter file so the doc stays self-consistent.
- [ ] **AC4 — Doc-only change, no behaviour impact:** No game code, SFX behaviour, or runtime audio pipeline is changed; existing §7.3 SFX scope and the shipped ToneForge pipeline remain authoritative for the MVP.
- [ ] **AC5 — Validation:** A new docs guard `src/audioDesignChapterDocs.test.ts` (following the sibling `*Docs.test.ts` convention, e.g. `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`) asserts, and passes, that: (i) `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists; (ii) it carries all 8 numbered sections plus Appendix A and Appendix B of the approved reference structure; (iii) GDD §7.3's "Background Music" subsection links the chapter **and** still states music is out of MVP scope; (iv) the GDD §8 "Background music" row links the chapter. All links resolve, and any index/table-of-contents entries are updated.
- [ ] **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (docs-only; confirms no accidental code impact).

## Constraints

- Music remains **"design reference, out of MVP scope"** — no change to the existing scope stance in GDD §7.3 or §8.
- The chapter is a **synthesis**, not a verbatim import (Q4/Q5, this session): the **musical content** is the producer's original retro-arcade brief reproduced faithfully (Source material (A)); the **document structure** follows the approved reference brief (author: Ross; version 1.0; dated 16 October 2026 — Source material (B)). The reference brief's Tableau card-game substance is **not** carried over.
- Follow the repo's docs naming/style conventions where sensible (singular Markdown addendum under `docs/`, referenced by relative link).
- UK English throughout.

## Existing state

- GDD §7.3 "Audio Direction" covers MVP SFX: baked ToneForge WAV pipeline, SFX event catalogue, per-enemy/per-player audio character, beat-synced explosion accents, and a one-paragraph "Background Music" subsection stating music is a nice-to-have, out of MVP.
- GDD §8 "Future Scope" lists "Background music — Synthwave / retro electronic soundtrack" with no further detail.
- No existing work item implements or specifies background music; the work log contains no musical-identity design doc.

## Desired change

- Add the Audio Design Chapter (AI Hell musical content in the approved reference structure) as a standalone GDD addendum document.
- Point GDD §7.3's "Background Music" subsection and §8's future-scope row at the new document.
- Keep all gameplay/SFX/runtime behaviour untouched.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (new) — the Audio Design Chapter addendum (confirm filename at implementation)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 "Background Music" subsection updated with a link + scope note; §8 "Background music" row updated with a link
- `src/audioDesignChapterDocs.test.ts` (new) — docs guard following the sibling `*Docs.test.ts` convention
- `./README.md` (if it indexes docs) — optional link to the new chapter

## Related work

- **Update GDD audio design section and code comments (AH-0MTGS9DZ6001IFJR)** — completed; historical GDD §7.3 SFX additions, unrelated to music direction.
- **Update audio documentation (AH-0MUTYV9QV0000HDT)** — completed; ToneForge baked-asset pipeline docs; source of the current §7.3 scope language.
- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item.
- See also GDD §7.3 and §8, and `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` for the authoritative SFX cue catalogue.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-stance divergence (medium):** the chapter is "APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION" in tone while the GDD keeps music out of MVP. Mitigated by AC2/AC3 explicitly framing the chapter as design reference; implementation remains a future work item.
- **Middleware references (FMOD/Wwise) are forward-looking:** the game currently uses Phaser/Web Audio with baked assets (§7.3). The chapter's §9 middleware guidance is design intent for future integration, not an instruction to adopt FMOD/Wwise in the MVP. Noted in the chapter context if needed.
- **Content divergence from shipped SFX:** the chapter (§6.4) proposes procedural SFX recipes that differ from the shipped baked-ToneForge SFX catalogue. The chapter is an addendum; §7.3 remains authoritative for MVP SFX (per constraint). Recorded as an assumption.
- **Scope creep:** producer may later want chapter sections mapped into the live audio system — that is future implementation work, tracked separately, not part of this docs-only item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where in the GDD should the 'Music & Thematic Audio Design' content live? (a) replace the §7.3 'Background Music' paragraph with the full chapter; (b) keep the paragraph and add a new top-level section; (c) other." — Answer (user): "A — below is a full brief for the music. Use this to create a new file and refer to it from 7.3." Source: interactive reply. The final decision refines (a): rather than inlining, create a **new file** (`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`) and **refer to it from GDD §7.3**; adopted as AC1/AC2.
- Q2: "MVP scope statement for music — (a) keep music 'design reference, out of MVP scope'; (b) promote into MVP." — Answer (user): "A." Source: interactive reply. Adopted as the chapter's scope framing (AC2/AC3).
- Q3: "§8 Future Scope 'Background music' row — (a) update to reference the new chapter; (b) leave untouched." — Answer (user): "A." Source: interactive reply. Adopted as AC3.

### Plan-session clarifications (2026-10-23)

- Q4: "What should `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` actually contain? (a) author an AI Hell Music System chapter from the producer's *original retro-arcade* content (Phrygian Dominant + Lydian, Combat Motifs A/B & Star Drift, progressions, FM 2–4 op + chiptune notes) laid out in the approved reference brief's professional structure — the reference brief serving as format exemplar only; (b) import the reference brief verbatim as-is; (c) adapt the reference brief's content to AI Hell's palette; (d) freeform." — Answer (producer): "**1. a**". Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Research: the reference brief describes **Tableau**, a candlelit card game (D Dorian, harpsichord, cello, FMOD, card-table SFX) and is therefore not AI Hell's musical content — AI Hell is a retro-arcade bullet-hell (GDD §1: inspirations Galaxians/classic arcade shoot-'em-ups). The intake session on 2026-10-16 flagged this same conflict and the question was never answered, which left AC1 unverifiable until now. Adopted as the corrected **AC1**.
- Q5: "AC1 enumerates ten sections including *Recommended Scales & Modes* and *Playtesting & Iteration*, but the approved reference brief actually has eight numbered sections plus two appendices and contains no *Playtesting & Iteration* section. (a) correct AC1 to the brief's real structure; (b) keep the ten-section enumeration and build the chapter to it." — Answer (producer): "**2. a**". Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Evidence: reference brief table of contents (Source material (B)). Adopted as the corrected **AC1**.
- Q6: "The full source brief is not embedded in the work item (only section names are), so an implementer cannot reproduce content faithfully and AC1's verbatim requirement is unverifiable. (a) recover the full text from the 2026-10-16 intake session log and embed it in the work item; (b) producer re-supplies the brief." — Answer (producer): "**3. a**". Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Evidence: recovered from session log `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell--/2026-10-16T11-00-00-344Z_herdr-1792148399-1716826-22311.jsonl`. Adopted as **Source material (A)** below plus the reference-brief record held in this item's comments.
- Q7: Producer additionally instructed: "Also create a follow up work item to implement the design." — Answer (producer): directive recorded verbatim. Source: interactive reply, this plan session. Adopted as follow-up implementation work item **Build the music system from the Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** tracked separately (dependency: the implementation is blocked by this docs item), consistent with the *Scope creep* risk entry and the out-of-MVP scope stance (AC2/AC3).

### Source material (A) — producer's original *Music & Thematic Audio Design* brief (verbatim)

This is the authoritative **musical content** for the new chapter. Reproduced verbatim from the producer's original prompt (2026-10-16). UK-English and retro-arcade framing must be preserved; formatting artefacts in the original (runs such as `♭7Example (E)`) may be repaired into readable Markdown without changing substance.

```markdown
Music & Thematic Audio Design

This section defines the musical identity of the game, focusing on scales, motifs, harmonic language, and usage guidelines across gameplay states. The goal is to merge retro‑arcade space tension (Asteroids) with relentless survival energy (Vampire Survivors), using a coherent musical palette that supports procedural layering and dynamic intensity shifts.

🎼 1. Core Musical Identity

The soundtrack is built around two complementary scales:

Primary Combat Scale — Phrygian Dominant

Used for: wave combat, boss spawns, high‑intensity survival phases.

Scale Formula: 1 ♭2 3 4 5 ♭6 ♭7Example (E): E – F – G♯ – A – B – C – D

Why:

Retro‑arcade tension

Exotic, driving, instantly “space danger”

Works extremely well with FM bass, square leads, and arpeggiators

Provides strong melodic hooks with minimal notes

Secondary Ambient Scale — Lydian

Used for: menus, starfield travel, upgrade screens, low‑intensity exploration.

Scale Formula: 1 2 3 ♯4 5 6 7Example (C): C – D – E – F♯ – G – A – B

Why:

Bright, floating, cosmic

Contrasts the combat scale without breaking aesthetic cohesion

Ideal for pads, shimmering arps, and soft synth textures

🎵 2. Melodic Motifs

Motifs are intentionally short (2–6 notes) to support looping, procedural recombination, and chiptune‑style repetition.

Combat Motif A — “Incoming Wave”

Scale: Phrygian Dominant (E)Contour: Rising tension → abrupt dropNotes: E – F – G♯ – F – E – DUsage:

Triggered at the start of each enemy wave

Can be fragmented into E–F–G♯ for micro‑stingers

Works well as a 3‑note arpeggiated alert

Combat Motif B — “Survival Pulse”

Scale: Phrygian Dominant (E)Rhythmic Cell: Dotted + straightNotes: G♯ – A – G♯ – F – EUsage:

Mid‑combat loop

Easily reharmonized for intensity scaling

Can be doubled with FM bass for crunchy retro drive

Ambient Motif — “Star Drift”

Scale: Lydian (C)Contour: Floating, circularNotes: C – E – F♯ – E – D – CUsage:

Menu screens

Upgrade/shop interface

Slow arpeggiated background texture

🎹 3. Harmonic Progressions

Retro arcade music often avoids complex harmony, but these progressions provide structure while staying loop‑friendly.

Combat Progression (Phrygian Dominant)

E – F – E – D

Minimalist, modal, tense

Works with pulsing bass and rapid arps

Can be expanded to E – F – G♯ – F – E – D – C – D for boss phases

Boss Progression (Phrygian Dominant, extended)

E – C – D – F – E

Chromatic tension

Strong “danger escalation” feel

Supports heavy FM brass or distorted square leads

Ambient Progression (Lydian)

C – D – E – F♯

Bright, drifting, spacey

Works well with pads and slow-moving textures

Can be looped seamlessly or expanded to C – G – D – F♯

🔧 4. Implementation Notes

Motifs should be stored as atomic musical objects (interval sets + rhythm cells) for procedural recombination.

Combat layers should increase harmonic density (more voices, faster arps) rather than changing the motif.

Ambient layers should use long‑release envelopes and minimal rhythmic content.

FM synthesis (2–4 operators) and chiptune waveforms (square, triangle, noise) define the retro palette.

All motifs should be designed to loop cleanly at 1–2 bars for dynamic layering.
```

### Source material (B) — approved reference brief (structure exemplar)

The full 58 KB reference document (Ross, v1.0, 16 October 2026) that defines the **chapter structure** is recorded verbatim in a comment on this work item titled *Source material (B) — approved reference brief (structure exemplar), verbatim*. It describes the card game **Tableau**; treat its **section architecture, table layouts, parameter/stinger/matrix formats and glossary style** as the template, and its **musical and SFX substance as out of scope**.

## Verification approach

Docs-only change, but the repo convention is that cross-cutting docs slices ship with a `*Docs.test.ts` guard
(12 sibling guards exist, e.g. `src/powerUpWeaponRosterDocs.test.ts`, `src/enemyRosterDocs.test.ts`). The guard
for this item asserts file existence, the reference-brief section structure, and both GDD cross-links —
including the "out of MVP scope" sentence, so a future edit cannot silently promote music into the MVP.

Manual checks that complement the guard:
- Open `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` and confirm every Source material (A) element maps into the document
  (two scales, three motifs, three progressions, four implementation notes) — nothing dropped, nothing invented.
- Confirm no Tableau substance leaked in (no D Dorian as the home mode, no harpsichord/cello ensemble, no
  card-table SFX).
- Confirm §7.3's SFX catalogue, autoplay and rate-limiting text is untouched (AC4).

AC6 is satisfied by the standard dev-push gate (full suite); the guard above gives the changed-scope signal.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** – Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD (interactions, impacts, enemy actions, advanced telegraphing) (completed)
- **AH-0MUTYV9QV0000HDT** – Update audio documentation (completed)
- **AH-0MTGS9DZ6001IFJR** – Update GDD audio design section and code comments (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: audio, design, gdd, music, update
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: audio, design, music, update
- `README.md` — matched: audio, design, gdd, update

# Scripted Gameplay Videos: generated-level scenes (Option C follow-up)

Multi-scene scripted capture (Option A, AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC) can only target **dev gym scene keys**. Option C lets a scene entry target a **freshly generated shipped-game `PlayScene` level** — the literal brief: *"create a level, play it for x seconds, capture y seconds"* — so one compiled video can showcase real, varied shipped gameplay rather than dev-only gyms.

## Problem statement

The multi-scene capture driver records any number of scenes with a single continuously-running `MediaRecorder` and 0.25 s page-side fades between them, but its `target` vocabulary is the watchable **gym** registry (AH-0MVFC6WPS004UOLO / AH-0MVFC70GT000B96J). A gym is a fixed, hand-authored dev scene: useful for showing a mechanic in isolation, but not the shipped game, and not "a level someone would actually play".

The shipped game plays **procedurally generated campaign levels** (`buildSequencedLevels` seeded per run, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`). Capturing those needs two things that do not exist yet:

1. a page-side way to start a **fresh generated run in-place** (no navigation, because a reload ends the recorder), and
2. a **multi-wave-aware capture window**, because a level is not a fixed-length showcase: wave 1 of level 1 is deliberately easy, waves end and transition on gameplay signals, and the bot can end the run before the configured window elapses.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can list generated game levels in the scene config and have one command record them into a single compiled video, so a promo shows real, varied shipped gameplay instead of dev gyms.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Wants showcase footage that looks like the shipped game: multiple generated levels, each with real waves, weapons, power-ups and enemy mixes, compiled into one clip.
- **Secondary — prospective players / viewers.** The audience of the showcase: they should see sustained, varied action in real gameplay, not dev gyms and not dead air between waves.

**Example user stories:**

- As the maintainer, I can add a `PlayScene` entry to `scenes.json` with a seed and a campaign level, so one command records that generated level for x seconds of play and y seconds of capture.
- As the maintainer, I can mix gym scenes and generated-level scenes in the same config, so one video shows both controlled mechanic demos and real gameplay.
- As a viewer, each level segment shows sustained action across waves, with a clean 0.25 s fade between segments, so the video reads as one coherent piece.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Generated-level scene target in config.** A `scenes[]` entry may target the shipped game: `target: "PlayScene"` with an optional `seed` (uint32) and an optional `level` (integer within the campaign, 1–`LEVEL_COUNT`), defaulting to a fresh random seed and level 1 when omitted. The config is validated **before** any Vite server or browser boots, failing fast with `Scene config error: …`, exit 1, and stable codes (mirroring `SCENE_CONFIG_ERROR_CODES`) for: a non-integer or out-of-range `level`, a non-finite or out-of-range `seed`, and any generated-level-only field (`seed`, `level`, `minWaves`, `maxCaptureMs`) supplied on a **gym** target (rejected rather than silently ignored). Every existing gym-only config (including `examples/scenes.json`) keeps working unchanged, and the new codes are asserted in tests.
- **AC2 — In-place fresh-run switching, one recorder, one visible scene.** The dev-gated director starts a **fresh** `PlayScene` run inside the already-running page — no navigation, no reload — so the single `MediaRecorder` spans every scene. Level entries run in demo (bot-driven) mode using the persisted bot-tuning configuration, matching `npm run capture`. Starting a capture scene **stops the previously active capture scene** and the new scene is the visible one regardless of Phaser registration order (a lazily-added gym scene otherwise renders **above** the boot-registered `PlayScene`), so gym→level, level→gym and gym→gym switches all record the requested scene. The director stays inert in production builds (`import.meta.env.DEV` gate; `npm run check-bundle` still passes).
- **AC3 — Dev-gated start-level and run-progress seams.** `PlayScene` honours a `startLevel` scene-start value **only in dev builds** (ignored in production) and begins the run at that campaign level the same way checkpoint resume does (`WaveManager.beginGame(level)`), with the run seeded from the entry's `seed`. A dev-gated page-side progress handle reports the live run's level/wave position and whether the run has ended, so the capture driver can observe waves without reaching into Phaser internals. Both seams are unit-tested, including the production-inert guarantee.
- **AC4 — Multi-wave-aware capture window.** A generated-level scene honours `captureMs` **and** an optional `minWaves` (default 2): the capture window extends past `captureMs` until `minWaves` waves have started, hard-capped by `maxCaptureMs` (default 3 × `captureMs`) so a stalled run cannot hang the capture. If the run ends first, the window ends early and the scene reports `endedEarly: true` plus the waves actually captured — a truncated segment is **not** a capture failure. Window accounting is pure and unit-tested against fake wave/clock samples (including the cap and the early-end cases).
- **AC5 — Single stitched WebM, unchanged A/V contract.** Generated-level and gym scenes may be mixed in one config. Output remains exactly **one** WebM at 960×540 with the game's own SFX, `video/webm;codecs=vp9,opus` (existing fallback order), with a page-side fade to black and back (0.25 s each way) between consecutive scenes, and the existing fade probe verifies the fades **in the recorded video**. The `--json` payload reports per scene `{ target, seed, level, playMs, captureMs, startMs, endMs, wavesCaptured, endedEarly }` alongside the existing `fadeMs`, `totalMs`, output path and fade/non-trivial verdicts.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents the generated-level target, the `seed` / `level` / `minWaves` / `maxCaptureMs` fields, the demo-mode note, the start-level seam and the `--json` additions; `README.md`'s capture section and `examples/scenes.json` gain a generated-level example.
- **AC7 — Tests and gates.** Hermetic (browser-free) tests cover config validation/normalisation, the wave-window accounting, the director's level-target pass-through and key validation, and the production-inert gates; the full project test suite passes (`/skill:test`), `npm run build` and `npm run check-bundle` stay green, and all related documentation (code comments, README, docs) is updated. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **One recorder, one page.** Level switching must happen **in-page**; a navigation or reload ends the `MediaRecorder`, so "record each level separately and stitch later" is the wrong shape.
- **No forked gameplay.** Generated-level scenes must play the **shipped** `PlayScene` code path (same scene class, same wave generation, same bot input seam) — no scene-class generation, no duplicated gameplay bodies; the gym↔game parity convention (AGENTS.md; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) must stay green.
- **Dev-only plumbing.** The start-level seam, the progress handle and any director changes are dev-gated; the production bundle and `npm run check-bundle` are unaffected.
- **WebM only.** No `ffmpeg` transcoding on this path.
- **Reuse Option A machinery.** Config validation, the scene plan/timeline, the fade overlay, the recorder/probe plumbing and the `--scenes` driver are extended, not duplicated.
- **Reuse the setup pass-through shape.** The blocking epic AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6 introduces `start(key, setup)` (a config `setup` object forwarded as `scene.start(key, setup)`); this item reuses that pass-through rather than inventing a parallel mechanism.
- **One visible capture scene at a time.** Scene stacking is out of bounds: the director must stop the previous capture scene (and/or guarantee the new one renders on top), because Phaser's `SceneManager.start()` only restarts the target scene (`node_modules/phaser/src/scene/SceneManager.js`) while `render()` draws every running scene in **registration** order.

## Existing state

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` — pure multi-scene core: `parseSceneConfig` / `loadSceneConfig`, `WATCHABLE_GYM_SCENE_KEYS`, `PARAMETERISED_GYM_SCENE_KEYS`, `SCENE_CONFIG_ERROR_CODES`, `buildScenePlan`, `buildSceneSampleTimes`, `evaluateSceneFadeSamples`, `buildScenesPayload`. Imports nothing (shared by bare Node and the bundle).
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` / `.d.mts` — hermetic contract tests and types; the watchable registry is pinned against `src/scenes/gym/` on disk.
- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` — dev-gated `window.__aiHellCaptureDirector.start(key)`; `resolveSceneKey` validates against the shared registry plus page discovery; registers a gym scene class with the scene manager before starting it.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — the `--scenes`/`--config` path: `runScenesCapture` → `captureScenes` (audio tap, composite overlay, one `MediaRecorder`, `driveSceneSequence`, fade probe, single-file write, `--json` payload).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — shipped gameplay scene. `init(data)` already accepts `{ demo, seed, demoDwellMs, resume }`; a run is created by `create()`, which resets run state, resolves/seeds the RNG (`_initRunSeed`) and calls `waveManager.beginGame(resume?.level ?? 1)` — the same seam a `startLevel` value would use.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — `beginGame(level)`, `level`, `levelName`, `waveNumber`, `waveCount`, `globalWaveIndex`; `globalWaveIndex` is the campaign-wide regular-wave counter a window can be driven from.
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` / `src/core/runEndedSignal.ts` — the established dev-gated `window` handle and dev-gated page-signal patterns (`window.__aiHellScenario`, `aihell:run-ended`, `window.__aiHellRunState`).
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — **Watch Demo** starts `PlayScene` with `{ demo: true }`; demo mode drives the shared bot input seam (`PlayScene.getBotInput`).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — the capture documentation this feature extends (multi-scene section, config schema, `--json` shape, "How it works").

## Desired change

1. A scene entry can name a **generated level**: `target: "PlayScene"` plus `seed` / `level` (and the level-scene window fields `minWaves` / `maxCaptureMs`).
2. The dev-gated director starts a **fresh demo run** of that level in-place (`scene.start('PlayScene', { demo: true, seed, startLevel })`), stopping the previous scene, so one `MediaRecorder` spans every scene.
3. `PlayScene` accepts a **dev-gated** `startLevel` start value (production-inert) and begins at that campaign level via the existing `beginGame(level)` seam.
4. The driver observes wave progress from a dev-gated page handle and computes each level scene's **capture window** from `captureMs` + `minWaves` (hard-capped), stopping early and reporting `endedEarly` if the run ends first.
5. The output contract is unchanged: one stitched WebM with 0.25 s fades, extended `--json` fields, and documentation plus an example config.

## Design questions (OPEN — awaiting producer answers)

The intake brief above is drafted against the **recommended** option in each case; the answers change the ACs, so intake is not complete until they are resolved (see the Appendix for the full record).

1. **Config shape for a generated-level scene.** *(Recommended: A)* — A) reuse the existing entry with `target: "PlayScene"` + `seed` / `level` fields, sharing the epic's `setup` pass-through; B) add a `kind: "gym" | "level"` discriminator per entry; C) a separate top-level `levels[]` list merged into the plan. (The answer also fixes whether the level fields sit inside a `setup` object or beside `playMs`/`captureMs`.)
2. **Which level, and therefore whether a start-level seam is in scope.** *(Recommended: A)* — A) allow an explicit `level` (1–`LEVEL_COUNT`) through a dev-gated `startLevel` seam, so clips can show mid-campaign intensity; B) level 1 only, no `PlayScene` change (cheap, but deliberately easy opening waves); C) derive the level from the seed (varied, but not addressable in config).
3. **Multi-wave window semantics and run-end handling.** *(Recommended: A)* — A) `captureMs` + `minWaves` (default 2), hard cap `maxCaptureMs`, run-end truncates and reports `endedEarly` (not a failure); B) wave-count driven only (`waves: n`, `captureMs` ignored for level targets); C) wall-clock only (`captureMs`), run-end simply stops the recording.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs` — extend entry validation/normalisation with the generated-level target and its fields; add pure capture-window accounting (`wavesCaptured` / `endedEarly` / cap); extend `buildScenesPayload`. Add stable error codes for the new failure modes.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.d.mts` — types for the level entry, window accounting and payload additions.
- `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` — hermetic tests: level config validation/normalisation, window accounting (normal / capped / early-end), payload fields, backward compatibility with gym-only configs.
- `src/core/captureDirector.ts` — level-target support: start a fresh demo run in-place, stop the previous scene, expose the dev-gated run-progress handle; keep production inert.
- `src/core/captureDirector.test.ts` — director tests with a fake scene manager (no browser): pass-through of `{ demo, seed, startLevel }`, previous-scene stop, progress handle.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — dev-gated `startLevel` start value (mirrors checkpoint resume's `beginGame(level)`) and a read-only run-progress accessor; production ignores the value.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — `--scenes` driver: drive generated-level scenes through the director, poll the progress handle, apply the wave-aware window, extend the `--json` payload and the fade/verdict reporting.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — document the generated-level target, fields, demo-mode note, seams and `--json` additions.
- `README.md` — capture section gains the generated-level capability.
- `examples/scenes.json` — a generated-level scene entry example.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scene stacking (confirmed, blocking).** Phaser's `SceneManager.start(key)` only shuts down/restarts the **target** scene, and `SceneManager.render()` draws every running scene in **registration** order. The current director therefore leaves each previously started gym scene running (hidden CPU + shared-`AudioContext` audio leak), and — because `PlayScene` is registered at boot *before* any lazily-added gym — a generated level started after a gym would render **underneath** the still-running gym. Mitigation: the director must stop the previous capture scene (and/or `bringToTop` the new one); captured separately as the blocking item **Capture director does not stop the previously running scene (scene stacking)** (AH-0MVNWJ5FH006QD8V), with per-direction switch assertions (gym→level, level→gym).
- **Bot survival on later levels.** A more intense level can end the run (defeat) before `captureMs`; the window must truncate cleanly *before* the game-over screen is recorded, and report `endedEarly` rather than failing.
- **Fade/verdict interaction.** An early-ended level segment shortens the recorded timeline, so the fade probe windows (and `totalMs`) must derive from measured wall-clock scene starts, as the Option A driver already does — never from the plan alone.
- **Determinism is content-level, not frame-level.** The run seed makes generated wave content reproducible per config; frame timing, audio and bot micro-jitter are not byte-identical. Clips are re-recordable but not byte-reproducible.
- **Dev-gate creep.** The start-level seam and progress handle must be provably inert in production (`check-bundle` plus a unit test that the production branch ignores `startLevel`).
- **One-recorder fragility.** Any code path that navigates, reloads or recreates the page silently truncates the video; the driver must never do so for a level scene.
- **Scope-creep risk.** In-UI level selection, a level editor, per-level camera framing, per-level audio mixing, and capture of mid-level *saved* runs are out of scope; record such opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption:** a "generated level" means campaign level `1..LEVEL_COUNT` of a fresh `PlayScene` run whose wave content comes from `buildSequencedLevels` seeded by the entry's `seed` (not a hand-authored `LevelDefinition` — that is the gym `GymLevel` path covered by AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6).
- **Assumption:** generated-level scenes always run in demo (bot) mode with the persisted bot-tuning configuration, matching `npm run capture`.
- **Assumption:** polling a dev-gated progress handle is sufficient for wave awareness — no new event bus/`CustomEvent` is needed.
- **Assumption:** `minWaves` counts *started* regular waves (`globalWaveIndex` increments), and the default hard cap of 3 × `captureMs` is generous enough for the slowest shipped wave without allowing an unbounded capture.
- **Assumption:** the recorded segment for a level scene starts at the level's first wave (after the level banner) and the banner itself is acceptable in the clip; suppressing the banner is out of scope unless the producer asks for it.

## Related work

- **Config-defined scene setups for scripted gameplay capture** (AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6) — `open`, `plan_complete`, **blocker** (`dep add` edge: this item depends on it). The epic's `start(key, setup)` pass-through and validated `setup` object is the mechanism this item reuses for `PlayScene` launch data.
- **Capture director does not stop the previously running scene (scene stacking)** (AH-0MVNWJ5FH006QD8V) — `open`, **blocker** (`dep add` edge; `discovered-from:AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX`). Confirmed during this intake; it must land for a level scene to be visible after a gym scene.
- **Scripted Gameplay Videos** (AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC) — `completed`. Multi-scene capture (Option A); records the deferred "A now, C later" decision that created this item.
- **Multi-scene capture driver: one recorder, fades, single WebM** (AH-0MVFC70GT000B96J) — `completed`. The driver this item extends (`runScenesCapture` / `captureScenes`).
- **Dev-gated in-page capture scene director** (AH-0MVFC6WPS004UOLO) — `completed`. `window.__aiHellCaptureDirector.start(key)`, the handle this item extends.
- **Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene** (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY) — `completed`. The bot-driven demo mode a generated-level scene records.
- **Checkpoint save/resume** (AH-0MVCRBTNF000DK51) — `completed`. Precedent for starting a run at a specific campaign level (`beginGame(level)`).
- **Deterministic run seeding and seed plumbing** (AH-0MUY08V6W001SJJN) — `completed`. The `seed` that makes a generated level reproducible.
- **Emit dev-gated end-of-run signal** (AH-0MUXZ4BXK001QCEK) — `completed`. The run-end observation the early-truncation path builds on.
- **Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration** (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL) — `completed`. The bot-tuning parity a level scene inherits from demo mode.
- **Create full video playthroughs** (AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU) — `completed`. Single full-run capture; the source of the bot/demo plumbing reused here.
- **Compile an action video** (AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX) — `completed`. Edits already-captured footage into a promo; consumes this item's output, does not block it.
- **Spike: automated gameplay video capture (headless browser + scripted bot)** (AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK) — `completed`. The original pipeline.
- **Capture: export action-intensity series + join anchor** (AH-0MVDV4DMY001Z7CU) — `completed`. Action-intensity telemetry that could later drive highlight selection from these clips.

## Appendix: Interview Q&A

- **Q1 (Map, to producer): How should a generated-level scene be named in the scene config?**
  Options: **A** *(recommended)* reuse the existing `scenes[]` entry — `target: "PlayScene"` plus `seed` / `level` fields, sharing the epic's `setup` pass-through; **B** add a `kind: "gym" | "level"` discriminator; **C** a separate top-level `levels[]` list merged into the plan.
  Rationale (why A is recommended): smallest diff, keeps one validation/pass-through path shared with AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6, and every existing config keeps working byte-for-byte.
  **OPEN QUESTION** — answer pending (producer). Evidence/context: predicted key files above; epic AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6 AC3 (`start(key, setup)`).
- **Q2 (Map, to producer): Should a level scene name a specific campaign level (which requires a dev-gated start-level seam in `PlayScene`), or always start at level 1?**
  Options: **A** *(recommended)* allow `level` (1–`LEVEL_COUNT`) via a dev-gated `startLevel` start value reusing `WaveManager.beginGame(level)`; **B** level 1 only, no `PlayScene` change; **C** derive the level from the seed.
  Rationale (why A is recommended): level 1's opening waves are deliberately easy, so a showcase would look like a tutorial; the seam is small and mirrors existing checkpoint resume.
  **OPEN QUESTION** — answer pending (producer). Evidence/context: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (`beginGame(resume?.level ?? 1)`), `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`.
- **Q3 (Map, to producer): How should the capture window behave for a multi-wave generated level, and what happens if the run ends first?**
  Options: **A** *(recommended)* `captureMs` + optional `minWaves` (default 2), hard-capped by `maxCaptureMs` (default 3 × `captureMs`), run-end truncates and reports `endedEarly: true` (not a failure); **B** wave-count driven only; **C** wall-clock only, run-end stops the recording.
  Rationale (why A is recommended): keeps the existing wall-clock contract, guarantees multiple waves of real action, and bounds a stalled or short-lived run without inventing a new failure mode.
  **OPEN QUESTION** — answer pending (producer). Evidence/context: `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (`driveSceneSequence`, measured fade windows), `runEndedSignal.ts`.

## Summary

Test-first slice for AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF: pins the drop-selection gate — the eligible set at six filled slots, and bit-for-bit unchanged draws below the cap. Written before the draw-path change so the gating implementation is driven by these tests.

## What is tested

- The shared draw seam (`drawNextDrop`-style helper in `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts`) over an injected rng: at six filled slots only owned kinds plus `availableWhenSlotsFull` entries can ever be returned, across a large seeded sample.
- Below the cap the same fixed rng seed reproduces the current draw sequence exactly (regression snapshot captured from the pre-change spawner), for power-ups and weapon drops alike.
- The all-zero-weight fallback is not used as the exclusion mechanism: a full pool with every weight zeroed still yields an eligible id, and weights for eligible ids are untouched.

## Deliverables

- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts` — gated draw + below-cap regression tests.
- `src/powerups/spawner.test.ts` — eligibility-filtered draw behaviour (including the all-zero-weight fallback and empty-selection guard).
- No production change in this item beyond what already exists (tests fail red until the draw gating lands).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Spawn gating at full slots — when all six slots are filled, the drop-selection path (game and gyms, one shared implementation) draws only from the six owned kinds plus every catalogue id flagged available-when-full (Extra Life and Mystery UFO are flagged by default); every other power-up and weapon id is never drawn. Verified here by a seeded/injected-rng unit test on the selection helper asserting a large sample of draws contains only owned or exempt ids.
- No behaviour change below the cap — while fewer than six slots are filled, drop selection covers the full catalogue exactly as today: a regression test with a fixed rng seed produces the identical draw sequence before and after the change (power-ups and weapons alike).
- The tests never rely on `Math.random` or wall-clock time; each injects an rng, and the empty-eligible-set case asserts a deterministic, crash-free fallback rather than the all-zero-weight first-entry fallback.
- Tests fail (red) before the gating change lands in "Gate the shared drop draw on the six-slot pool" and pass unchanged afterwards.

## Dependencies

Blocked by "Shared six-slot helper, cap constant and exemption flag". Blocks "Gate the shared drop draw on the six-slot pool".

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` (draw seam under test)
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`
- `src/powerups/spawner.ts`, `src/powerups/spawner.test.ts`
- `src/core/rules.ts` (`POWER_UP_WEIGHT_IDS`, `WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS`)

data.description:
Discovered during intake of Scripted Gameplay Videos: generated-level scenes (Option C follow-up) (AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX) — discovered-from:AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX.

## Problem

The dev-gated in-page capture director (`src/core/captureDirector.ts`, AH-0MVFC6WPS004UOLO) starts each requested gym scene with Phaser's **SceneManager**.start(key). Phaser's SceneManager only shuts down and restarts the **target** scene; it never stops the scene that is currently running (see `node_modules/phaser/src/scene/SceneManager.js` — `start()` calls `sys.shutdown()/sys.start()` on the requested scene only). So the existing multi-scene capture (Option A, AH-0MUX2NLFZ00128WC) leaves **every previously started gym scene running** behind the newest one: their update loops, timers, spawners and audio keep ticking for the rest of the recording.

Why it has gone unnoticed: gym scenes each cover the full 960x540 canvas and Phaser renders scenes in registration order, so the most recently *added* gym draws on top and the footage looks correct. The cost is hidden: wasted CPU on stacked scenes (a real soak/reliability risk) and any sound a stacked scene emits is mixed into the shared AudioContext the recorder taps.

It becomes a **hard blocker** for generated-level scenes (AH-0MVE01EY0008QEVX): `PlayScene` is registered at boot, i.e. **before** any lazily-added gym scene, so starting a generated level after a gym scene renders the level *underneath* the still-running gym — the recording would show the gym, not the level.

## Expected behaviour

- Starting a capture scene stops (or sleeps) whichever capture scene is currently active, so exactly one capture scene runs at a time — no stacked update loops, no leaked audio, no render-order surprises.
- The newly started scene is guaranteed to be the visible one regardless of registration order (stop the previous scene, and/or `bringToTop`), so gym → level, level → gym and gym → gym switches all record what was requested.
- Behaviour is unchanged for a single-scene capture, and production builds stay inert (`npm run check-bundle`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hermetic director test (fake scene manager, no browser) proves the previously active scene is stopped before the next one starts, and that no navigation/reload occurs.
- A test pins that the started scene is the top-most/visible one after a switch whose registration order differs (PlayScene registered at boot, gym added lazily).
- The multi-scene driver keeps one page and one `MediaRecorder` across the switch (no regression).
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` notes the one-scene-at-a-time guarantee; `npm run check-bundle` and the full suite pass.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes

- Coordinate with **Config-defined scene setups for scripted gameplay capture** (AH-0MVNW7U5G003SNO6) child C2 (**Director and registry: pass setup through start(key, setup)**, AH-0MVNW8UCZ004CY0R): both touch `src/core/captureDirector.ts`, so land whichever comes second on top of the other rather than in parallel.
- Small, additive change to existing shipped code — no gameplay behaviour change.

Smallest diff, one validation path, every existing config keeps working byte-for-byte.

**Q2 — Should a level scene name a specific campaign level (in scope: a dev-gated start-level seam in `PlayScene`), or always start at level 1?**
- **A (Recommended)** — allow `level` (1–`LEVEL_COUNT`) through a dev-gated `startLevel` start value that reuses `WaveManager.beginGame(level)` (the same seam checkpoint resume uses). Level 1's opening waves are deliberately easy, so a showcase would otherwise look like a tutorial.

- **C** — derive the level from the seed (varied, but not addressable in config).

**Q3 — How should the capture window behave for a multi-wave generated level, and what happens if the run ends first?**
- **A (Recommended)** — `captureMs` plus optional `minWaves` (default 2), hard-capped by `maxCaptureMs` (default 3 × `captureMs`); if the run ends first the window truncates and reports `endedEarly: true` (not a capture failure). Keeps the existing wall-clock contract, guarantees real multi-wave action, bounds a stalled run.
- **B** — wave-count driven only (`waves: n`; `captureMs` ignored for level targets).
- **C** — wall-clock only (`captureMs`); the run-end signal simply stops the recording.
